verses.text: If I should speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become a sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.

verses.text: And if I should have prophecy and should understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I should have all faith so as to remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.

verses.text: And if I should give away all my possessions, and if I should deliver up my body that I may boast, but have not love, I am profited nothing.

verses.text: Love is patient, it is kind; love does not envy, love does not boast, it is not puffed up.

verses.text: It does not act unbecomingly, it does not seek its own [things], it is not provoked, it keeps no reckoning of evil.

verses.text: It does not rejoice at unrighteousness, but it rejoices with the truth.

verses.text: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

verses.text: When I was a child, I was speaking like a child, I was thinking like a child, I was reasoning like a child; when I became a man, I have made null the [things] of the child.

verses.text: For now we see through a glass in obscurity, but then, face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know fully, even as I have been fully known.
